title: Multi-agent reinforcement learning discovers a dominant iterated-game strategy
summary: Multi-agent reinforcement learning was used to explore strategy space beyond classic iterated-game strategies such as tit-for-tat, generous tit-for-tat, win-stay-lose-shift and zero-determinant strategies. It yielded a memory-two bilateral reciprocity (MTBR) strategy that outperforms a wide range of strategies in pairwise interactions with high payoffs. In evolving populations MTBR is reported to dominate and to foster higher cooperation and social welfare in homogeneous and heterogeneous structures and across game types, verified by simulations and mathematical analysis. The result is theoretical and simulated, with no empirical human data.
ai_technology: Multi-agent reinforcement learning exploring the strategy space of iterated games

evidence.tested: Evolutionary simulations and mathematical analysis of the MTBR strategy against other strategies.
evidence.unknown: Whether MTBR matters for real human or organizational decision making; preprint not peer reviewed; full text not reviewed.
